sentences.text: The genus Kryptohadros includes only one species, Kryptohadros kallaiae, known from a partial skull and skeleton.
Its name combines Greek words for 'hidden' and 'bulky' to reflect its status as a previously unrecognized hadrosauroid in the Hațeg Basin.
The holotype specimen was found between 2022 and 2024 at the Fântânele-3 site in Hunedoara County, Romania.
János Magyar and colleagues formally described Kryptohadros kallaiae as a new genus and species in 2026.
The specific name kallaiae honors the mother of the describer, Csilla Kállai.
Evidence suggests the holotype belonged to an individual that had reached at least the subadult stage.
Phylogenetic analyses place Kryptohadros in the endemic clade Telmatosauridae, alongside Telmatosaurus and Tethyshadros.
Kryptohadros lived during the Maastrichtian stage, approximately 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
It is the second named non-hadrosaurid hadrosauroid discovered in the Hațeg Basin.
